{"en": [
"But now, on the other side, here we are, and it is incumbent upon us to argue in favor of our Sages.",
"To begin with the objections, we say that the supposed proof in support of the opponents from the account of Jeconiah's descendants, as explained in the previous chapter,",
"apart from whatever else might be said about it, can easily have its tendrils pruned with the shears of this answer:",
"that the anomalous verse in the middle of that passage, 'And the sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah,' etc. [1 Chr 3:21], breaks the thread of those generations and confuses for us the chain of their descendants,",
"so that one cannot learn the obscure from what is still more obscure. And although, according to Kimhi's commentary on those verses, the difficulty follows as we mentioned,",
"we do not set one man's opinion against a Mishnah, and it is not in his power to say 'accept my view' when other opinions too can find room for [the verse].",
"As for the supposed proof from the reckoning of the Persian kings, in all that is set out in chapter 38,",
"we say that since they [the Sages] of blessed memory did not accept that there were as many of them as the large total given by the historians whose words we cited, among whom in any case there was also disagreement,",
"and since we heard the angel say to Daniel, 'Behold, three more kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth' [Dan 11:2], the fourth possibly being fourth counting the said Cyrus, that is, the third itself, and no more,",
"it seemed right to them to bring the matter close to possible reality and to maintain the small number of those kings, saying: 'He is Cyrus, he is Darius, he is Artaxerxes' [b. Rosh Hashanah 3b],",
"all the more so since it is confirmed that the name Artaxerxes is a title fitting all the kings of Persia, as we mentioned.",
"However, the proof brought in favor of the opponents from the six priests mentioned in Nehemiah 12, in all that is written in chapter 37,",
"this, to my limited understanding, is certainly a difficulty for our Sages, who placed the generation of Simeon the Just immediately after the generation of Jeshua with no interval between.",
"And those who say that the verse 'And Jeshua begot Joiakim' [Neh 12:10] can be interpreted of Jeshua the Levite mentioned just before it—their words will not help,",
"first, because even if they were Levites, most of their generations would still be needed within that Persian kingdom for the long time that elapsed between Jeshua the high priest and Simeon the Just, who was born after them in the seventh or eighth generation after Jeshua, after Nehemiah's death;",
"and further, let them look and see that there is an explicit verse in this very passage: 'Joiakim son of Jeshua son of Jozadak' [Neh 12:26], as we mentioned in chapter 37.",
"Nor can one say that they of blessed memory knew by their tradition that all those six priests were in one and the same generation, Jeshua being extremely old and all those descendants of his serving as priests in his lifetime,",
"for of each of them in that passage separate days are written:",
"'in the days of Jeshua,' 'in the days of Joiakim,' 'in the days of Eliashib,' 'in the days of Joiada, Johanan'—and it is known that this is like 'in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah' [Isa 1:1], as stated in chapter 38.",
"And you already know what the Master, the Guide, wrote in part 2, chapter 17, against those who rely on forced answers:",
"that when the invalidity of the proofs has been shown, the soul grows weaker in believing what we wished.",
"Now although the Tosafists, chapter Yesh Noḥalin, s.v. 'Tarvaihu nami' etc., state",
"that at times some of our Sages were not expert in Holy Scripture—as in the case in chapter Ha-Parah, 'He asked me whether in the first Tablets it says \"that it may be well,\" and [I said] I do not know,' and the case of R. Abbahu about Rav Safra, in chapter Ḥelek, 'Did I tell you [he was expert] in Scripture?'—",
"it is certain that such a thing cannot be thought of R. Yose Berabbi, author of the statement of the 34 years, ⚠",
"and all the more so of all the Sages who follow him, and still more so when we see many of Ezra's verses expounded for all their purposes here and there.",
"But what seems right to me in this, until I hear something better said,",
"is that this matter, which seemingly is to be attributed to them of blessed memory as an error,",
"issued from them deliberately and with undeniable wisdom—namely, that they made themselves as though they knew nothing of the generations of those priests other than Jeshua and Simeon the Just, skipping all in between.",
"For whatever knowledge we require, whether out of necessity or for the advantage of good order, for whatever reason, and cannot attain,",
"it is wisdom, not error, to devise a convention for it which everyone will follow.",
"When our Sages saw that it was fitting to set a limit of time for the duration of the Second Temple, as had been set for the First,",
"and [saw that] from the kingdom of the Greeks until the destruction, by the Era of Contracts well known among the people,",
"it was known to be 380 years, besides the six in which they reigned in Elam, as we cited their words in chapter 23;",
"whereas what elapsed from its beginning until that time, in terms of the six high priests, was not specified in Nehemiah's words,",
"and they had not seen the books of the Jews Yedidyah [Philo] and Josephus in the Greek tongue, or did not believe them,",
"they made themselves as though they did not know those priests, or as if they were all in one generation,",
"and agreed to count in it for the Persian kings, saying: 'The Persian kingdom [lasted] 34 years in the time of the Temple' [b. Avodah Zarah 9a],",
"although it follows by implication that all eight generations of the said priests are swallowed up in them, which is far from reason, as we wrote in chapter 37.",
"And if you say: but for the Persian kings too their duration has been shown to be more years, as explained in chapter 38,",
"to this there are two answers. The first: when they saw that the totals of their many years were not written explicitly, they took from them only the part found explicitly,",
"namely the 32 years of Artaxerxes and about two years estimated between the statement",
"'and after some days I asked leave of the king' [Neh 13:6] and the year of the war in which he fell into the hand of Alexander;",
"and this is close to their well-known way: 'If you grasped a little, you have grasped.' The second follows from the reason Rabad gave for their counting the total of 410 for the First Temple up to the third year of Jehoiakim:",
"that since the kingdom of Judah from then until the destruction was low and harassed, they saw fit not to reckon it.",
"For you should know that although the Persians, with God's help, subdued the kingdom of Babylon, as is known, many years passed for them without their kingdom being firmly established,",
"but they were constantly harassed, whether by foreign wars they had with the other kingdoms of the earth,",
"or by internal ones among those holding power, thrusting one another aside by main force and the edge of the sword.",
"And this is very clear to whoever reads the works of the writers Xenophon and Herodotus, each in his first book,",
"who related of Cyrus that he killed the son of the queen of the Scythians in war, and for this the queen, his mother, rose against him with a great army and broke him breach upon breach,",
"and when he came into her hand she cut off his head and put it in a vessel full of the blood of the slain and said over it: 'Behold, you thirsted for blood; blood you shall drink until your soul is sated.'",
"True, this was before the Temple was built; but you will find in the two writers mentioned, and at length in Xenophon, that for many years afterward too many wars continued among the Persians themselves, each seeking to be heir to the throne,",
"and we have already cited the chief points of his words on this in chapter 30.",
"Now when these considerations were accepted in whatever way by them of blessed memory, whose custom, as stated, was to count only the years of quiet and settled kingship,",
"they counted for the said Persian kings only the 34 years apparent from the verses, as mentioned,",
"but not with the opinion that together with the years of turmoil there were not more.",
"And this is similar to what I wrote near the end of chapter 38 in the name of the sage Don Isaac [Abravanel], that our Sages did not deny that the Persian kings were more than three; see there and draw the analogy.",
"Is this not their explicit statement: 'The Persian kingdom in the time of the Temple,",
"the Greek kingdom, the Hasmonean kingdom, and the house of Herod'? By this they meant that these were the portion of their years known for certain, while conceding also doubtful years of which they did not speak.",
"And from that statement went forth the report about the duration of the years of the Temple, that they were 420, combining the days of these four kingdoms.",
"And although before Artaxerxes Scripture mentions the six years of building under Darius,",
"since Artaxerxes is a doubtful name, whether proper name or title,",
"it seemed good to them, as we mentioned, to say that it was a title of the said Darius, for in this too 'if you grasped a little, you have grasped' [i.e., the fewer years],",
"and once this was settled for them, they attributed to him by way of midrash the title Cyrus as well, because he was a worthy king, and said: 'He is Cyrus, he is Darius,' etc.",
"Besides, perhaps they saw in all this a further necessity, since they had posited in Seder Olam ch. 28 that the seventy weeks [Dan 9:24] include the seventy years of exile,",
"and if so, only 420 of them remained for the duration of the Temple.",
"In any case it was wise of them of blessed memory to fix pegs in the count of the years of the Second Temple as well, for the peace of mind of later generations, so that the total sum would agree with the tradition in our hands.",
"And it became a praiseworthy rule among the scribes in every generation to write in all kinds of documents 'the year such-and-such according to the count we count,'",
"for in this way everything follows the practice established of old.",
"In any case it is very clear that the deficit or surplus relative to the truth itself—what was, was—",
"will not harm us at all in the fixing of months, festivals, and the intercalation of years, as will be further shown in this chapter.",
"Especially since, even if it were granted as true that it would disturb the order of the calendar—which in fact it does not—",
"behold, blessed be our God forever, who, wishing to give Israel merit, granted us much grace in saying 'This month shall be for you' [Exod 12:2]—'which you shall proclaim' [Lev 23:2],",
"and the true tradition came in the Yerushalmi and chapter 2 of Rosh Hashanah, 'even if deliberately, even if inadvertently, even if misled,' over which R. Joshua said to R. Akiva, 'You have comforted me.'",
"Likewise, although, in the words of the divine author of the Kuzari at the beginning of Discourse 2, the Sabbaths of the Lord and the festivals of the Lord depend on the inheritance of the Lord,",
"and because of the sphericity of the earth the inhabitants of the other climes are not equal to it in the time of sunrise and sunset,",
"as the author of the Ma'or wrote on chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah regarding the verse 'And there was evening and there was morning, one day' [Gen 1:5], which implies the whole duration of the day,",
"and Ibn Ezra on the verse 'And the sun rose upon him' [Gen 32:32]—He, may He be blessed, so that no outcast be banished from His people, wrote of all the said holy times 'in all your dwellings,'",
"to indicate that He accepts them from every person wherever he is, as also appears to the sage Ibn Ezra on the portion Ha-Ḥodesh.",
"Apart from these matters, we have further to consider in this regard what I shall now say.",
"It has already been explained in Maimonides' Laws of Sanctification of the Month, ch. 5, how the sanctification of months by sighting and the intercalation of years by the signs explained there in ch. 4 continued in Israel until the end of the Sages of the Gemara, as he says:",
"'From when did Israel begin to reckon by this calculation by which we reckon today?",
"From the end of the Sages of the Gemara, from the time the Land of Israel was laid waste and no fixed court remained there",
"(meaning ordained [judges] in the Land of Israel, for the Sanhedrin had already ceased, as we cited his words in chapter 25);",
"but in the days of the Sages of the Mishnah, and likewise in the days of the Sages of the Gemara until the days of Abaye and Rava, they relied on the fixing of the Land of Israel.' End quote.",
"For so he derived from what is said at the end of chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah: 'Rava used to sit fasting two days; once it turned out as he [suspected]' [b. Rosh Hashanah 21a],",
"meaning that he would fast on the Day of Atonement two days and nights lest the court had made the month full.",
"And what he did not tell us—who initiated this calculation—",
"we have heard from the Gaon Rabbenu Hai, as mentioned by the Nasi R. Abraham in Sefer ha-Ibbur, discourse 3, gate 7,",
"and from Nahmanides in his glosses on the enumeration of the commandments, positive commandment 153, who wrote as follows:",
"'Today there is no ordained court in all Israel; but the remedy for this difficulty is that R. Hillel the Nasi, son of R. Judah the Nasi, who instituted the calculation of intercalation, sanctified months and intercalated the years fit to be intercalated according to his count, until Elijah comes and we return to [fixing by] sighting.'",
"And at the end of the passage he wrote: 'And on this basis are the months and festivals fixed today, until he comes and teaches righteousness.'",
"Also the great astronomer R. Isaac Israeli in his book Yesod Olam (in keeping with what we mentioned above in chapter 25; see there) wrote in discourse 4, ch. 9, as follows:",
"'R. Hillel son of R. Judah the Nasi and the court, who were ordained and close to the end of the Sages of the Gemara, instituted and fixed for us the new moons and festivals and intercalated the years for all time and season, from then until the teacher of righteousness comes,",
"and they did this so that the law of fixing would not be abolished with the abolition of ordination,",
"for once he and the court agreed, I read [the verse] \"which you shall proclaim\" as applying to the generations.",
"And at first R. Hillel and the court resolved to found for us the lunar cycle of 19 years and to arrange in it the years of intercalation in the order GWḤ ADZṬ [3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 17, 19], so that the 17th of Nisan would always fall in the new season,' etc.,",
"as he also wrote in his book Sha'ar ha-Shamayim, lesson 32, as follows:",
"'The sanctification of the month and intercalation of the year were conducted throughout the earlier period by the ordained court, as they saw fit, whether according to calculation or the needs of the hour,",
"yet they endeavored to intercalate precisely seven years in every 19 years,",
"for thereby the solar and lunar years are equal at all times and the festivals always come in their proper season.' End quote.",
"And you, understanding reader, if you look at the first chapter of the astronomy of al-Farghani the Arab, whether in the Latin translation or the Hebrew translation,",
"you will likewise find that all the Arab nations dwelling in the 'land of the gazelle' then counted—and one may believe they still count—their months by the moon according to the mean motion, as in R. Hillel's arrangement, one full and one defective, ⚠",
"with some months intercalated to correct the fractions, for they too count whole days;",
"and he said that for this reason they begin their day from sunset, since that is the time the moon appears.",
"If, then, this order began among our people from the time of the said R. Hillel,",
"as long as no error has occurred since—and certainly none has occurred, the proof being the Era of Contracts—",
"our new moons, the intercalations of our years, and all the festival days made by his corrected calculation according to the secret of intercalation, whose basis is that there are 1 day, 12 hours, 793 parts [beyond full weeks] between conjunction and conjunction, and seven intercalations in every 19 years, as stated,",
"are without doubt regular in their order and performed according to their law. And as for what was earlier, when [months] were sanctified by sighting, we need have no concern at all,",
"for although you find in them of blessed memory that the court would calculate to know whether testimony could possibly be accepted,",
"that calculation of theirs was only, in the words of Maimonides, Laws of Sanctification of the Month chs. 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 and the end of 18,",
"concerning the conjunction of the two luminaries in their true motion, which is in the zodiac, as he explained at the end of ch. 11,",
"which calculation, according to his words in those chapters, was precise, in the manner of the astronomers who know the positions of the stars;",
"and this is what we learned in chapter 2 of Rosh Hashanah: 'They ask the witness: How did you see the moon, before the sun or after it?",
"How high was it and how wide?' etc.; 'Rabban Gamaliel had diagrams of the shapes of the moon,' etc.—",
"not the calculation of the said R. Hillel called ibbur, which is according to the uniform motion of the star in its sphere, called mean motion, in the words of the said Maimonides at the end of ch. 11, for which we need none of these investigations.",
"But it suffices that we know Rabban Gamaliel's tradition that between conjunction and conjunction there are 29 days, 12 hours, 793 parts, for the purpose of fixing the months, as you find in the said Maimonides, ch. 6 of the Laws of Sanctification of the Month,",
"and from this we shall not budge until Elijah comes, as Nahmanides said, 'and we return to sighting,'",
"and in the words of Israeli which we cited, 'until the teacher of righteousness comes,' as Ibn Ezra also wrote in the portion Emor, the section on the festivals, as follows:",
"'Our Sages transmitted to us that in exile we should rely on the intercalation built on the mean motion, and we cannot do anything better than it.'",
"And although you find in Rabbenu Ḥananel, as cited by Rabbenu Baḥya on the verse 'This month' and on 'from year to year,' that their calculation then was likewise that of R. Hillel, you will notice that not for nothing did the said great sage Maimonides, who is the later authority, diverge from his words,",
"as we also mentioned in chapter 35 in connection with the words of Ibn Latif.",
"And this, in my opinion, because you would ask him: we know the words of Ibn Ezra in the portion Ha-Ḥodesh, as follows:",
"'At times there will be between the conjunction of the ibbur (that is, by R. Hillel's order) and the true conjunction, sometimes more and sometimes less, nearly 14 hours.' End quote,",
"so that what the sage al-Farghani wrote in the first chapter of his astronomy is correct, that often the new month according to the mean motion (which is the way of the said ibbur) falls on one day and according to sighting on another;",
"if so, what need had they of the calculation of the ibbur, when the word of the Lord is thus: 'See and sanctify'?",
"And the proof he brought from the verse 'on the day after the new moon, the second' [1 Sam 20:27]—you will find there that the mighty Rashi and Kimhi refute it.",
"And you will find it explicitly in the sage Ibn Ezra, portion 'These are the festivals of the Lord,' as follows:",
"'When the Temple stood, the festivals were entrusted to the court, as it says of Hezekiah's Passover, \"And the king took counsel,\" etc. [2 Chr 30:2].",
"And there is no proof in all of Scripture as to how Israel fixed the months and festivals.",
"And what the Gaon said, that they relied on the calculation of the ibbur, is not true,",
"for in the Mishnah and also in the Talmud there are proofs,' etc. See there, for he spoke at length and well,",
"especially about the years intercalated from the sign BHRD. As for the Jubilees, we already know that even by the time of the first destruction they were not observed,",
"and the slight commemoration now kept of the sabbatical years is not from the Torah, as Maimonides explained in ch. 10 of the Laws of Shemittah.",
"Also in the responsa of R. Levi ibn Ḥabib, no. 143, who investigated which year is our sabbatical year, he wrote at the beginning of his words as follows:",
"'Since the Shemittah is one of all the commandments of the Lord which are not performed in this exile of the host,",
"for the release of land applies only in the Land, and by rabbinic law,",
"and the release of debts, though we became obligated in it outside the Land too by rabbinic law,",
"it has already become the custom in our places to collect a bond over which the seventh year has passed, whether this is a legally valid custom on account of the strengthening clauses of bonds or an error,' etc.",
"And after he wrote shortly thereafter as follows: 'There is a dispute among the decisors whether the sabbatical year was the year 86 of the sixth millennium, or 87, or 88, or 89,' etc.,",
"he wrote at the end of the responsum as follows: 'Are we obliged to observe all the said doubtful years or not?",
"I say that since the obligation of Shemittah after the destruction is only rabbinic, and we hold that a rabbinic doubt is ruled leniently, we need observe only one year in remembrance of the Sabbatical.' End quote.",
"Thus, apart from the fact that whatever cannot be known has the fixed nature of which one says 'your head and the mountain,' ⚠",
"the doubts are numerous even about the rabbinic commandment, so that even if we wished to observe the Shemittah according to the accepted reckoning,",
"we would not know what to do, except to choose for ourselves one year for the honor of the Torah, until the teacher of righteousness comes.",
"However, I foresee, as if by astrology, that the objector's contradiction will again rise against me, and he will say: Do we not see in the Laws of Sanctification of the Month, Maimonides ch. 6, Semag no. 47, Tur Oraḥ Ḥayyim 428, and all the choicest later sages, that they teach us to find the conjunctions according to the count of years and cycles from BHRD, saying that this is the conjunction that occurred in the first year of creation?",
"And if the number of years from creation is less or more, then BHRD is not the true sign, and it turns out that we have all gone astray like sheep [Isa 53:6] in the calendar, we and they.",
"I shall answer you, my brother: in Semag in particular, who explains his words more than all of them, you will see that he wrote as follows:",
"'For the seasons we hold like R. Joshua, that the world was created in Nisan, on Sunday, and at the beginning of Wednesday night the luminaries were suspended; and because of the moon's accusation and rebuke it tarried 7 days, 9 hours, 642 parts,",
"and when you add to it retroactively 2 days, 4 hours, 438 parts, you will find the Tishrei conjunction of Tohu, which was before Nisan, on Monday night at 5 hours, 204 parts, which is the said sign BHRD.' End quote.",
"Now consider: apart from what is well known, that this conjunction is imaginary, posited for the Tishrei of the year preceding the creation of the world, which did not actually exist—for which reason it is called 'of Tohu'—",
"you should wonder at his first foundation, that the world was created in Nisan, which he derived from their words in Seder Olam ch. 4 and chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah, 'for the Flood like R. Eliezer, and for the seasons like R. Joshua':",
"if their intention was that this was how it actually happened, that it was created in Nisan,",
"how can one testify of a woman that she gave birth and the next day her belly is between her teeth—saying afterward that for the Flood, that is, for the beginnings of years, it was created in Tishrei?",
"These are two things that contradict each other; their judgments cannot both be right.",
"Further, you would face a contradiction of law against law, for the prevailing view among them of blessed memory is that it was created in Tishrei, for so they ordained for us, chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah, in the Musaf prayer: 'This day is the beginning of Your works,'",
"and this is the truth, as Ibn Ezra proved in the portion Be-har Sinai and Nahmanides on the verse 'This month,' with sound proofs,",
"which you can also strengthen and confirm by the Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel on the verse 'in the month Ethanim' [1 Kgs 8:2]: 'the month the ancients called the first (that is, before the Exodus, as Kimhi explained, Kings 9) and now it is the seventh,'",
"that is, after the commandment 'This month shall be for you,' etc. The said Nahmanides too already mentioned this proof in a fine sermon about twelve leaves long, which I have in hand, on the festival of Rosh Hashanah,",
"and he likewise mentioned it in the commentary on the portion of the Flood, where he also brought a proof from the words of the Mekhilta, 'This month shall be for you—and Adam did not count by it'; therefore he did not trouble to mention it again in its place, the portion Ha-Ḥodesh.",
"Likewise the said view is supported by the anonymous teaching of the tractate on idolatry, 'When Adam saw the day growing ever shorter,' etc., for had it been Nisan, it would have been growing ever longer;",
"and it is further supported by their agreed statement in chapter Eḥad Dinei and chapter Elu Terefot, which is also found in the chief of the Christian sages [Augustine] in his City [of God], book 15, ch. 12, as we mentioned in chapter 17:",
"'All the works of creation were created in their full stature and form'; for, as they of blessed memory said in Bereshit Rabbah 14, Bemidbar Rabbah 12, and Shir ha-Shirim Rabbah on the verse 'Go forth and see' [Song 3:11], Adam and Eve were created as if twenty years old,",
"by which they meant that they were not like day-old infants but grown and tall of stature.",
"Likewise their statement in chapter 1 of Avodah Zarah and the said Ḥullin ch. 3: 'The ox that Adam offered—its horns preceded its hooves,'",
"by which they meant, as appears there from Rashi's explanation, that it was formed complete, so that when it emerged from the earth first its head with its horns appeared and afterward its hooves;",
"so too the other creatures, and especially the produce of the earth, were created complete, for 'the tree bore its fruit,' etc. [Joel 2:22],",
"and this, then, would be in Tishrei, in which falls the Feast of Ingathering, not in Nisan.",
"Also from their statement in the Yerushalmi of Rosh Hashanah that the names of the months came up with them from Babylonia, it was understood that the name Tishrei indicates beginning, for the Targum of 'See, I have begun' [Deut 2:31] is ḥazi sharitei,",
"as R. Maimon also wrote at the beginning of his commentary on the book of al-Farghani, the abridgment of the Almagest.",
"Rather, certainly their statement 'for the seasons like R. Joshua' is merely posited by convention and choice,",
"whether to begin auspiciously, as the commentator on the Laws of Sanctification of the Month wrote in ch. 9 as follows:",
"'Why was the new year for the seasons in Nisan and not in Tishrei? Because one makes a beginning only from a fair and pleasant time, namely when the sun is at the head of Aries,' etc.,",
"or for some other reason—not that they thought it true that the world was created in Nisan.",
"If so, Semag, who wrote at length 'and at the beginning of Wednesday night the luminaries were suspended,' etc.,",
"and likewise the sage Abudarham, who wrote in the gate of conjunctions as follows: 'We have a tradition from our fathers that the sun and moon were created at the end of the month of Adar,' etc., in all his long words found there,",
"appear to have deviated from the straight path, as is also clear from the words of the Ran on chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah, on [the mishnah] 'they pass before Him like benei maron.'",
"And the said sage Abudarham did not interpret well in calling this 'a tradition from our fathers,'",
"all the more so if he meant by this 'from Sinai'; for according to Maimonides, ch. 1 of the Laws of Rebels, Rabad ha-Levi at the beginning of his Sefer ha-Kabbalah, and the Tosafist in chapter He-Arel on 'R. Shimon—I say it is a halakhah,' matters of tradition have no dispute in their roots, though it is possible in their branches,",
"whereas here, on the very root of the law and the substance of the event, R. Eliezer disputes R. Joshua.",
"And again you will wonder at this, that Semag said that because of the moon's accusation and rebuke it tarried 7 days, 9 hours, 642 parts:",
"granted that we say it is enough for the rebuke of the Shekhinah to be like the rebuke of a father, seven days,",
"what have these 9 hours and 642 parts to do with the said cause? Besides, their statement about the moon's accusation is but a splendid invention to alert us to various teachings, as I wrote at the end of chapter 15,",
"in which they made themselves as if fitting the verses, which on a superficial view present a difficulty in saying 'the great luminaries' and afterward 'the lesser luminary,' and 'a sin-offering to the Lord' [Num 28:15], in their well-known manner of 'I am expounding a verse';",
"it is not credible that in their opinion it actually happened as written, that the moon was abashed and hid itself, so as to give an efficient cause for the said tarrying.",
"For even granting, with the Master, the Guide, part 2, ch. 8, that the spheres are living and intelligent, we know there is no rivalry among them, as it is written, 'He makes peace in His heights' [Job 25:2];",
"and if so, this is a notion from the lips outward, which they did not truly maintain, and far be it from the said master to set it before us as a true thing! Moreover, the said conjunction BHRD you will not find among the Sages of the Gemara anywhere,",
"and in all that R. Eliezer wrote at length in his chapters 6, 7 and 8 about the courses of the luminaries he mentioned only the said 1 day, 12 hours, 793 parts, and the 4 days, 8 hours, 876 parts, and 10 days, 21 hours, 204 parts that derive from it,",
"for even in his time, when they sanctified by sighting, they made use of such [figures].",
"And what Maimonides wrote in ch. 5 of the Laws of Sanctification of the Month, as follows: 'It is a halakhah to Moses from Sinai that at a time when there is no Sanhedrin, they fix by the calculation by which we reckon today'—",
"Nahmanides already objected to it in commandment 153, as follows:",
"'The Master made the matter a tradition and a halakhah to Moses from Sinai—something not said in the Gemara and not mentioned anywhere.' End quote.",
"Likewise you will not find among his commentators, who indicate the sources of the laws, anyone who has shown us whence he got this statement.",
"But we shall say in his defense that his intent concerns our obligation to obey the court in time of emergency, as in what R. Hillel did.",
"But concerning BHRD and the signs derived from positing it as the conjunction—WYD and 3 [days] 10 [hours] 876 [parts], which we shall mention shortly, or 7 [days] 9 [hours] 642 [parts] and 4 [days] 9 [hours] 642 [parts]—you will find nothing in the said R. Eliezer;",
"on the contrary, there is a dispute about the said BHRD, which would not be so had it been received by a tradition of prophecy,",
"for some count to the conjunction WYD [Friday, 14 hours] in the Tishrei in which Adam was created,",
"and some count to the conjunction 3 [days] 10 [hours] 876 [parts] for the Tishrei of the second year after Adam's creation, as you will hear further on.",
"But with good consideration it will become clear to you that both the sign BHRD and the two other signs we mentioned, according to whoever holds any of the three,",
"are nothing but an innovation of the arranger of the said calculations, like all the other signs given in the calendar,",
"and like the division of the hour into 1080 parts because it is convenient for arithmetic, though a mnemonic for it is found in the verse 'who had understanding of the times' [1 Chr 12:33];",
"that is, that sage reckoned from his time backward to the creation of the world according to the total he posited for creation, in the way we too reckon from our time backward to know past conjunctions,",
"and at the end he arrived at 3 [days] 10 [hours] 876 [parts] for the second Tishrei, the sign WYD for the Tishrei of Adam's formation, and BHRD for the conjunction of Tohu,",
"each of which likewise results for anyone among us who investigates it, from whatever year of his years he begins to count;",
"and so he fixed the pegs at one of the said signs, for each according to his own view among the three opinions mentioned,",
"and on that foundation, according to the total agreed for creation, the conjunctions are always found in order.",
"And truly, had it occurred to the said arranger that the years of the world were even ten thousand more,",
"he would likewise have gone on reckoning with the surpluses of the cycles to the end of that reckoning backward, as stated,",
"and if, for example, GHRM had resulted instead of BHRD, that is what would be before our eyes today,",
"and likewise had he reckoned them fewer than the total we count, he would have completed his course and fixed [the sign] from the end of the time reckoned by him.",
"Do you not see the sage Abudarham, in the said order of intercalation, who took the trouble to arrange each and every remainder up to a thousand cycles, which are 19,000 years, and said that 1 day, 14 hours, 1000 parts is the remainder for a thousand cycles,",
"by whose many signs you can know any future conjunction to the end of several thousand years, as long as you add the remainder fixed for it to the conjunction of your days;",
"and likewise by that method of his you can reckon and know backward up to a million imaginary years before creation, by subtracting.",
"And with this consideration, which is indeed easy for those who know the practice of mathematicians in giving signs on their roots,",
"the addition or subtraction of years to creation causes no fault at all in the calendar, as I shall go on to explain.",
"For no sage among those who seek truth should imagine that in fixing the sign BHRD, or either of the other two signs according to those who hold them, as stated, the arrangers proceeded from the earlier to the later,",
"that is, that they knew by prophecy or a tradition from Sinai that it was truly the first conjunction, and that from it they reckoned and continued the calculation of all conjunctions that have come or will come,",
"so that you would say that by adding even one month you displace BHRD from its place and annul the words of prophecy from which it came to us;",
"for this is indeed very far from reason. Especially when you consider these observations which I shall tell you.",
"First, my brother, you should notice that the years counted in the Torah or the Prophets, which we gather to know their sum to creation,",
"cannot reasonably be believed to have all been always exactly complete, from moment to moment,",
"so that you would say that all the generations counted from Adam to Noah, to Abraham, to the Exodus, the 480 years until the building, and the years of the kings of the First Temple—together nearly fifty figures—began exactly at the start of a year and ended at its close;",
"on the contrary, we have trustworthy witnesses that many of them were counted as partial [years].",
"First, consider that their statement in chapter 1 of Sotah on the verse 'I am a hundred and twenty years old today' [Deut 31:2]—'my days and years are complete; this teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, fills the years of the righteous from day to day and from month to month, as it says, \"the number of your days I will fill\" [Exod 23:26]'—",
"is excluded in the case of the ten generations from Adam to Noah, since they were wicked, as is known,",
"besides that the intent of the statement concerns the time allotted for their lives, even if it ends in the middle of the year.",
"From this you will understand that just as the years counted for them until death do not imply that they were exact to their end,",
"so those counted for them until begetting, as it says 'And So-and-so lived so many years and begot So-and-so,' from which we gather the totals of years to creation, are not to be understood as exactly at the end of the year,",
"but fell short or exceeded by months, about which the holy spirit was not particular.",
"And if you say these months were evened out either in the father's last year or in the son's first,",
"you will notice that in this way you impair the plain sense of the text both in the father's years and in the son's,",
"for these exceed and those fall short by months of the total written in the book.",
"Further consider that in chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah we hold 'all agree,' etc.",
"And further, in chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah we hold that all agree Isaac was born on Passover,",
"and likewise the Exodus was in the middle of the year, and it is written of it, 'And it came to pass at the end of 430 years' [Exod 12:41].",
"Also their entry into the Land in Joshua's days was at Passover, and it is written in Joshua, 'For forty years they walked,' etc. [Josh 5:6],",
"and the building of the Temple was begun in the second month, and it is written of it, 'in the 480th year after the going out,' etc. [1 Kgs 6:1],",
"and the destructions of both Temples, according to them of blessed memory, were in the tenth month after Tishrei, and 410 and 420 are counted for them.",
"And regarding the years of the kings of the First Temple, you find of Ahaziah, 'and he reigned over Israel two years' [1 Kgs 22:52],",
"and Kimhi wrote there as follows: 'They were not two full years, etc., but since Ahaziah did not complete the second year, it counts it for him [and also] for his brother and his father.'",
"And Rashi wrote there as follows: 'I checked and found with most of the kings of Israel that [Scripture] is not exact in counting their years, and if he came to power at the end of a year it counts it at his beginning and does not count it for him elsewhere.' End quote,",
"just as in the book of Ezra, concerning the discrepancy of several totals in the passage 'These are the people of the province,' which is doubled in that same book, Rashi wrote as follows: 'Scripture was not exact in the reckonings,' etc. And this should not be loathsome to us, for so the seventy souls who went down to Egypt were by the plain sense only 69, and yet the total of seventy is written of them,",
"and Benjamin was born in the Land of Israel, and nevertheless it writes of all of Jacob's sons that they were born in Paddan-aram,",
"and Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, and with all that it says, 'With seventy souls your fathers went down' [Deut 10:22],",
"and the slain sons of Gideon were only 69, for Jotham escaped, and even so in three places it counts them as seventy,",
"all as in Ibn Ezra's words on the portion Vayigash, the portion Ki Tissa, and in the commentary on Nehemiah 7.",
"Likewise Nahmanides in his glosses, root 1, labored much to prove that this is the way of the Torah, our prophets, and our rabbis,",
"and in the Nimmukim of R. Isaiah of Trani on the Torah you will find, at the beginning of the portion Noah regarding the days of the Flood, that he wrote as follows: 'It is the way of Scripture to take a round number even if a few are lacking or extra.'",
"Apart from this, it is likewise clear from Scripture that besides the full years counted in the First Temple for the kings of Israel,",
"one must count one month in which Shallum son of Jabesh reigned, and six months for Ahaziah. ⚠",
"In any case there is no cause for concern here, for it is a judicial measure not to be concerned about details, since, in the words of the Yerushalmi of Rosh Hashanah which we mentioned in chapter 35, the large number swallows the small and it becomes as nothing.",
"Likewise in Seder Olam ch. 4 you will find explicitly as follows: 'We learned from Scripture that once a day has entered into a month, it is counted a full month,",
"and a month that has entered into a year, it is counted a full year, for part of the month is like all of it and part of the year like all of it.'",
"You also know that according to Scripture the 480th year after the Exodus was itself the fourth of Solomon and the first of the building of the First Temple,",
"and nevertheless you have seen Rashi in chapter 1 of Avodah Zarah, regarding the 1380 years which we mentioned in chapters 23 and 35,",
"counting it with those preceding the building and counting after it 410 years of the Temple,",
"and this is in the manner of the year of the Flood, about which they disagreed in Bereshit Rabbah 32 according to Rashi's explanation; see there.",
"Likewise I mentioned to you in chapter 35 the words of the author of the Terumah, no. 135, on the years of the Second Temple, that in one respect it would be proper to count them as 409 and in another as 421, etc.",
"Thus necessarily, if one imagines that in the whole number of years elapsed from the beginning of creation until today one must add—not only the years the commentators mentioned regarding the Exodus, as mentioned above in chapter 35,",
"and the twenty years by which, according to the other commentators named in the said chapter 35, the days of the First Temple were longer, or the first eight [years] of Hosea, which we also proved there were omitted, according to all, from the total of 410—",
"but even one single month missing from its sum, or which we would need to subtract from it on account of some partial year counted as complete;",
"then certainly it would be necessary on its account to subtract one [interval of] 1 day, 12 hours, 793 parts from BHRD or add it,",
"and so many times over for several months, and necessarily BHRD would be displaced from being the head of the reckoning counted for us.",
"But if we say that this BHRD was posited for an agreed total by the arrangers of the calculation, you will find everything in order and coming out well, with no breach and no stranger among us.",
"For R. Hillel and his court, when they came to set a beginning for the count of years and to found their calculations on it,",
"wished to tie it to the creation of the world, as we mentioned in chapter 25, not to the Greek kingdom, nor to the destruction, nor to anything else customary of old;",
"when they set their minds to gather the totals of years from creation to their time,",
"they certainly knew and recognized everything that could be in doubt,",
"both in the number of years written in the Torah on account of the months, if one imagines that they fell short or exceeded,",
"and in the length of the Egyptian exile and the duration of the First and Second Temples, as stated.",
"And they likewise saw and recognized that it is impossible to arrive at the truth itself, for who will cross over for us to the far side of past time and clarify it for us?",
"And the verses bear the differing opinions found about them, without our having a prophetic tradition to decide among them,",
"for with such a tradition disputes would certainly not have arisen, and the Gaon Rabbenu Ḥananel, the pious Nahmanides, and others would not have dared to dispute Seder Olam about the 2448,",
"nor Rabad ha-Levi, Kimhi and their colleagues about the 410. So R. Hillel, like the sage who knows the interpretation of a matter [Eccl 8:1], chose and agreed to take in his calculation all the figures as they were found current in the nation, without second thoughts about this or that, whether to add or subtract,",
"and on the total collected by him from them all by this convention he founded all his calculations, for everything pertaining both to past time and to the future, from his days until the teacher of righteousness comes.",
"And on the basis of these words you will say that R. Hillel, in understanding and wisdom, accepted this convention regarding the sum total of years, just as he also agreed to adopt the calculation of the mean conjunction instead of sighting after the true one, since this had become impossible for us, there being no ordained court in the Land,",
"and just as it was agreed to reckon the seasons from Nisan and the conjunctions from Tishrei, although the world was created in only one of these two times,",
"and to follow the reckoning of the seasons customary among us although it is known to be open to question, as we shall mention further on.",
"For a thing that is not absolutely possible, we must do as best we can,",
"and of what is by its nature doubtful we do not say 'it is this,' except by way of our convention.",
"And exactly the same holds had it seemed fitting to R. Hillel and his court to set a smaller or larger total for the years of creation: they would have set up for us the other marker that would have resulted at the end of their backward count.",
"And the statement about the moon's accusation in Ḥullin ch. 3—whose authors truly intended by it to alert us to various teachings, as we mentioned above in chapter 15, and as some later authorities also mentioned, especially Rashba and R. Reuben son of R. Ḥayyim Zevi, regarding other statements, in their commentaries on aggadot—",
"fits rightly the arrangers of the calculation according to the words of Semag that we mentioned,",
"for they found in it the semblance of a cause and a support for extending BHRD of the Tishrei of Tohu to 7 [days] 9 [hours] 642 [parts] of the following Nisan, when you add to it 2 [days] 4 [hours] 438 [parts], with the season preceding [the conjunction] by the measure of the days of its rebuke.",
"The second [observation] is a reliable proof that the sign BHRD, or another as mentioned, is a tradition of wisdom derived backward from the total of the years of the world agreed upon by the arrangers of the calculation, not from prophecy and a tradition from Sinai:",
"namely what you find in the sage commentator on Maimonides' Laws of Sanctification of the Month, ch. 6, who wrote that three opinions are found about the beginning of the years of the world:",
"the Westerners begin from BHRD, the conjunction of the Tishrei of Tohu that preceded the formation of Adam, whether he was formed in the following Nisan, like R. Joshua, or in the following Tishrei, like R. Eliezer;",
"and accordingly the seven years of intercalation in each cycle will be GWḤ ADZṬ [3, 6, 8, 11, 14, 17, 19].",
"And the Easterners begin from the conjunction of the Tishrei of Adam's formation, which, according to the statement that the said commentator attributed to our rabbis, coincided with the said formation on Friday at the end of the 14th hour,",
"the mnemonic being WYD, or you may say WYB, which is Friday, 2 hours into the day—the same thing;",
"and accordingly the years of intercalation are BHZY GWḤ [2, 5, 7, 10, 13, 16, 18]. And of this view were Rabbenu Saadia and Rabbenu Hai, as appears in R. Abraham the Nasi's Sefer ha-Ibbur, discourse 3, gate 7, in the author of the Ma'or on chapter 1 of Avodah Zarah, and in Ibn Ḥabib's responsum on the Shemittah, no. 143.",
"Also, according to what the author of Ḥeshev ha-Efod wrote in ch. 22, the reckoning of 2448 in Seder Olam must be counted not from the sign BHRD but from the sign WYD.",
"And some begin from the conjunction of the year after the formation of Adam, which was 3 [days] 10 [hours] 876 [parts], and the years of intercalation are ADW ṬBHZ [1, 4, 6, 9, 12, 15, 17],",
"and he wrote as follows: 'Although each of these three opinions is true, except that the one counts one year more to creation than the other,",
"(for so you will find in Rabbenu Saadia, in the said responsum, regarding his year 1238 of the reign of Alexander, that it was 4686 from creation, whereas others counted 4687),",
"most masters of the science of intercalation chose to begin from BHRD, so as not to discard the five days that preceded the formation of Adam.' End of his words.",
"Now, discerning reader, you can judge that if the said sign BHRD had come from Sinai, or was in any way a tradition of prophecy,",
"there is no doubt that the two other opinions would never have been mentioned or occurred to anyone, earlier or later, for why would they exchange it when it is correct as needed?",
"And its use among us would not have been by way of the majority's choice, as stated, but a fixed statute from all the generations and congregations of our fathers.",
"And I already wrote you at the end of chapter 35 the words of the said Rabbenu Hai Gaon, who said: 'The calculation one must rely on is the conjunction WYD, not BHRD; and that they established the conjunction BHRD is to teach the students,' etc.",
"And consider his saying 'they established' and 'to teach the students,' which resembles the words of Rabbenu Isaiah the Later on chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah, cited there by the author of Shiltei ha-Gibborim, who wrote as follows:",
"'Since the Great Court ceased, they do not fix by sighting,",
"but there is a calculation known to all the exiles, which the ancient sages instituted for them, and they all fix by it in one way,'",
"like which you will also find in the author of the Akedah, gate 50, discourse 5, as follows: 'The sages of the ibbur posited the conjunction BHRD, which, as is clear from their words, is the conjunction of Tohu.'",
"Also in this chapter I cited the words of Semag and Abudarham, that in their view the tradition concerned the conjunction of Nisan,",
"but since we needed to know the conjunction of the Tishrei of Tohu, we discarded from it 2 [days] 4 [hours] 438 [parts], and BHRD remained for us;",
"and I likewise cited the words of Nahmanides in the glosses, that nothing is found in any of our Sages' books calling these a tradition and a halakhah from Moses our Teacher.",
"Thus in any case no prophetic tradition came concerning BHRD or its two said companions; rather, it was agreed upon by the arrangers we mentioned.",
"And from this, together with every other testimony that will emerge for you from the rest of the chapter, you will understand that Rabbenu Baḥya's tradition about BHRD in his commentary on the verse 'And the earth was tohu' [Gen 1:2] (see there)",
"is not the foundation proper to the masters of truth, and you will also have from it a paradigm to apply to other cases.",
"Know, too, that the proof brought by the said commentator on the Laws of Sanctification of the Month in favor of those who begin from Adam's conjunction, Friday at the end of 2 hours—",
"their statement 'in the third He formed him,' so that the moon's conjunction and Adam's formation were found at one moment, the beginning of the third hour—",
"with all due respect to him, is a fabrication and a thing without legs.",
"For first, he did not set their words before us as they are,",
"for the statement 'in the third He formed him' is not seen or found in any book;",
"indeed, this statement of theirs is found in six places, and although there are some differences among them, they all agree in this, that not one of them speaks of the third hour as he does.",
"You find in ch. 11 of Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, and in Sanhedrin, chapter Eḥad Dinei—cited also by Rabbenu Baḥya in his commentary on the verse 'And the Lord God formed' [Gen 2:7]:",
"'In the first [hour] He gathered his dust, in the second He kneaded it, in the third He shaped his limbs, in the fourth He cast a soul into him,' etc.",
"And in Vayikra Rabbah 29, Tanḥuma at the end of the portion Shemini, Midrash Tehillim on 'A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day,' and the Pesikta on the verse 'Forever, O Lord, Your word stands fast in heaven' [Ps 119:89], which the Ran cited on chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah, you will find:",
"'In the first it arose in thought before Him, in the second He consulted the angels, in the third He gathered his dust,",
"in the fourth He kneaded it, in the fifth He shaped his limbs, in the sixth He made him a golem, in the seventh He cast a soul into him,' etc.",
"Thus in attributing to them of blessed memory this wording, 'in the third He formed him,' the said commentator bore false witness against our rabbis.",
"And the formation, whose true nature is the bestowal of his essential form, that is, the casting in of the soul,",
"according to all their said statements did not take place until after the said third [hour];",
"if so, the formation of Adam did not coincide with the moon's conjunction.",
"And even if you say that the gathering of his dust is considered formation, according to the Gemara of Sanhedrin and the said Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer it was in the first [hour],",
"and so the hour of his formation is not agreed but disputed—how then shall we make it a sure peg on which to hang the reckoning of all the days of the earth?",
"But the true reason of those who begin from the conjunction WYD (or, you may say, WYB, as mentioned above) is",
"that when you add 4 [days] 8 [hours] 876 [parts] to BHRD of Tohu, the conjunction of the following year will be WYB,",
"just as when you add 4 [days] 8 [hours] 876 [parts] to WYB, the conjunction of the third year will be 3 [days] 10 [hours] 876 [parts],",
"and thus the said conjunctions arise backward from one another if you go on subtracting;",
"therefore it makes no difference which of these beginnings you take in hand for the number to creation agreed upon by us, except for the addition of a year or two years, as stated above.",
"Further, you should consider that there is not one among the discerning who would not judge that in this statement of theirs, and in all like it, the inner meaning concerns fitting matters other than what appears from the plain sense,",
"and that whoever interprets it as it stands is an outsider. For you know that although the verses are clear that the works of creation were divided over the six days,",
"many of the world's sages, both of Israel and of the other nations, concluded that the truth is that all creation was at once, without distinction of time, as we mentioned in chapter 6 of discourse 1.",
"How then can you imagine, regarding the creation of man alone, who is like a breath [Ps 144:4], that He, may He be blessed, measured and reckoned for it twelve hours from morning to evening, or a noticeable majority of them,",
"all the more so when we see that Scripture relates that the beasts, cattle, and creeping things preceded his creation on that same sixth day.",
"And our rabbis in Bereshit Rabbah 12 said: 'Six things were created on the sixth [day]: Adam and Eve, creeping things, cattle, beasts, and fatlings,' ⚠",
"and surely these other four that preceded his creation also required a separate hour each, so that impure and pure would not be mixed together;",
"and if this is really what happened in their opinion, who told this from the beginning that we may know it? Among all the prophets there is none who tells or announces it.",
"But necessarily there are inner meanings for them of blessed memory in their said statement, and you will find the intent if you seek it,",
"as, say, their teaching that man is beloved by Him, may He be exalted, and that his creation is essential, so that, as it were, He labored over it a whole day,",
"in the manner of their saying about the whole world: 'With ten utterances it was created; and what does Scripture teach thereby? To exact punishment and to give good reward,' etc. [m. Avot 5:1].",
"In this way too you will understand the statement of R. Aḥa in Sanhedrin ch. 4: 'The formation of man was in His image, and out of fondness He lingered over it.'",
"And once this observation is clear to you, no doubt you will not take the plain sense of the statement as testimony of an event that happened.",
"Take this path also in every similar case, for then you will discern and understand how the foundation for arriving at the truth in such matters is, as they alerted us in chapter 15, to recognize the words of the sages and their riddles [Prov 1:6] as parable and figure,",
"as was also the custom of the ancient sages of the nations, who when speaking of matters of wisdom would hint through invented stories and deeds of gods, humans, or species of animals.",
"And this either to hide them from the masses, or so that the hearer would enjoy the imagined tale and thereby remember it,",
"or for other reasons, as the sage R. Judah [Leone Ebreo], author of the esteemed Dialogue of Philo and Sophia, wrote in its second dialogue.",
"True, when Pythagoras came he moved from those inventions to hints by means of numbers, arithmetic—one, two, etc.",
"And afterward, when Plato came, he moved from these too and confined his hints to geometrical figures, called in Greek geometrici, such as the circle and the square and their appurtenances,",
"as appears from him when he speaks about the elements, the soul, and other subjects besides;",
"yet the common element in all three said modes is that they are speech in parable and hint, which they describe as symbolic.",
"And in these ways, or ways close to them, and especially attached to verses, sweet sayings of our rabbis are found in many places.",
"The third [observation] is what you find in the sage Israeli in his book Yesod Olam, discourse 4, ch. 3, as follows:",
"'The third principle is BHRD, and its meaning is that it was revealed to our ancients of blessed memory through their research or by way of prophecy, and they knew that the moment of the first Nisan conjunction in the world, according to the one who says it was created in Nisan, fell at 9 hours, 642 parts,' etc.,",
"'and likewise they knew that the moment of the first Tishrei conjunction, according to the one who says it was created in Tishrei, fell at the end of the 14th hour of Friday,' etc.; see there.",
"Thus he said rightly that the said sign was revealed to our ancients through their research,",
"and it is known that human research proceeds from the later to the earlier, as we mentioned at the end of chapter 35.",
"And if, to magnify and glorify the wisdom, he added 'or by way of prophecy,' these are nothing but 'prophetic' words on his part,",
"for he turns out to admit that this is a prophecy of which we do not know whether it occurred or not,",
"all the more so since its prophet is unknown and it is itself doubtful. Indeed, you will marvel at his saying 'according to the one who says thus, and according to the one who says thus'—",
"have you ever heard of prophecies riding two horses like these? No doubt, had the prophetic emanation come to light its lamp over our heads in this inquiry about the first conjunction in the world,",
"we would likewise have seen by that light the true beginning of the months, whether it was Nisan or Tishrei, and no dispute would have arisen about it.",
"And the fourth, a seal of perfection [Ezek 28:12] that will add strength to what we have mentioned, will become clear to you if you incline your ear to what I tell you.",
"You know how great were the wisdom and stature of the great master Maimonides in all his words in general, and in the Laws of Sanctification of the Month in particular,",
"so that he—not, God forbid, as an arrogant man, but as seemed right to him—said of them at their end, 'Seek out of the book of the Lord and read' [Isa 34:16];",
"nevertheless you will find the said great sage Israeli, in his book Yesod Olam, ch. 9, discourse 4, writing as follows:",
"'Our master Moses thought to give a reason for [the rule] Lo ADU Rosh [Rosh Hashanah not on days 1, 4, 6] from the course of the two luminaries in their mean and true conjunction,",
"and that is what he wrote at the end of ch. 7 of the Laws of Sanctification of the Month: \"Why do we not fix by this calculation on days 1, 4, 6? Because it is for the conjunction of moon and sun in their mean motion; therefore they made,\" etc., \"so as to meet the day of the true conjunction.\"' End quote.",
"And there Israeli mentioned the Rabad's objection to him and supported it,",
"and labored to prove from the ways of astronomy that the said Maimonides' words make no sense. Likewise in the book Sha'ar ha-Shamayim, lesson 34, he wrote as follows:",
"'When ordination ceased at the end of the days of the Sages of the Gemara, the elders and sages of that generation stood up with the tradition they had from the prophets (and you have already heard our words about these prophecies),",
"and transmitted to us this corrected calculation for fixing the new moons and festivals, which is all built and founded on the course of the two luminaries in their mean motion,",
"and we now have no business in this with their true motion, as some sages thought, to the point of saying that the essence of the postponement of Rosh Hashanah depends on the true conjunction;",
"this is not true, as I proved in the book Yesod Olam.' End quote.",
"And in general he upholds the view of the Rabad that the reason for the postponement was so that the day of the willow would not fall on the Sabbath, nor the Day of Atonement on Friday or at the Sabbath's close,",
"as the Ran also wrote on chapter Benei ha-Ir,",
"although Semag, positive commandments no. 47, accepted the said opinion of Maimonides;",
"and there is a great practical difference, for according to Maimonides the postponement derives from the principles of astronomy,",
"whereas according to his opponents it is a convention by the court's power, granted by the verse 'which you shall proclaim,' as is known.",
"Also the sage commentator on the Laws of Sanctification of the Month, whom it befitted to defend the said master,",
"raised an objection of his own against the said principle at the end of ch. 3 and said that he has no answer for him until the teacher of righteousness comes.",
"Likewise, regarding the place on which the calculation of the times of the seasons and conjunctions is founded,",
"you will find in the said book Yesod Olam a great dispute with two groups of sages among our people,",
"for he wrote there, discourse 4, ch. 7, as follows: 'R. Ḥassan the Judge and R. Isaac ben Rakufial taught and said that this place which we seek to know is the eastern end of the inhabited world, and the master R. Abraham bar Ḥiyya the Nasi agreed with them in this,",
"and I, the author, held this opinion in the past, until I found that R. Isaac son of R. Baruch refuted their words and arguments,",
"and ruled and said that this place on which the calculation of the conjunctions and seasons was founded is not the eastern end, as they thought.'",
"And shortly after: 'And the author of the Kuzari, and likewise the author of the Ma'or, as I informed you (that is, the end of discourse, ch. 17, and discourse 4, ch. 3), said that the calculation of the conjunctions was founded on the middle of the Land of Israel, and these too strayed from the path of reason,' etc., ⚠",
"'and therefore it seems that in this matter one should rely neither on these nor on those,' etc.; see there.",
"And in the said discourse 4, ch. 3, after refuting, in his opinion, the words of the said Kuzari and Ma'or, he wrote as follows:",
"'And I investigated by way of study the times of lunar eclipses and found that the calculation of the times of the seasons and conjunctions is founded on the navel of the earth.' End quote.",
"So that on this question, according to his words, you have three opinions:",
"the first, of the Judge, Ben Rakufial, and the said R. Abraham, that this calculation was founded on the eastern end of the inhabited world;",
"the second, of the Kuzari at the beginning of discourse 2 and of the author of the Ma'or on chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah, that it was founded on the middle of the Land of Israel,",
"which the author of the Ma'or also called simply the navel of the earth, as though the Land of Israel were truly the middle of the world.",
"And likewise Maimonides, at the end of ch. 11 of the Laws of Sanctification of the Month and in his commentary on chapter 1 of Rosh Hashanah—cited also by the commentator on the Laws of Sanctification of the Month, ch. 7, regarding 'the new moon is hidden six [hours]'—",
"held this view, but explained clearly that Jerusalem is not in the middle of the world; see there.",
"And the third, of the said Israeli, that it was founded on the navel of the earth, that is, the navel of the true world, not the navel of the inhabited world, which lies in the northern quarter,",
"for which reason he wrote in the said book Yesod Olam, discourse 2, ch. 3, as follows:",
"'The point at which the line of longitude, which is the equator, and the line of latitude, which is the meridian, intersect each other at their halves is called the navel of the earth,",
"and you should pay much attention to this place of the inhabited world and know it, for we have much to do with it in this book.' End quote.",
"And I have already alerted you to his dispute concerning this navel in discourse 1, ch. 11.",
"And now, discerning reader, after informing you of all this,",
"go out and reckon and judge a fortiori: if, regarding the end of the calculation derived from BHRD, whose founding and arrangement took place only a short while ago, in the days of R. Hillel and his court—for our fathers were with them but yesterday, around the sealing of the Gemara, as mentioned—",
"these disputes, and others besides, arose among the said great tamarisks,",
"and though we know the calculation we do not know its foundation, so that with great insight Ibn Ezra raised the doubts recorded in his introduction to the commentary on the Torah, in the second way, and in the portions Ha-Ḥodesh and the festivals (see there);",
"how can your mind rest in believing that, regarding its beginning before the formation of our first father,",
"knowledge of it came to us proceeding from the earlier to the later, when not a trace of it is mentioned in the words of prophecy and the Gemara,",
"as I also informed you of Nahmanides' words in his glosses, that no source is found for this tradition?",
"How was this wondrous thing known, which the Lord had not spoken? Did He not, may He be blessed, say to Job and to all mankind with him, 'Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?' [Job 38:4], 'Do you know the ordinances of heaven?' [Job 38:33].",
"And the sage of the Kuzari, with great understanding, founded all his divine words in that work, as appears from it in discourse 1, on His saying, may He be blessed, at the head of His holy commandments, 'I am [the Lord your God] who brought you out,' etc. [Exod 20:2]—for all this was seen by you eye to eye—",
"and not 'who created heaven and earth,' lest you say, 'We do not know this, which neither our fathers nor our fathers' fathers saw.' Rather, the truth of the matter of the sign BHRD is certainly as we said:",
"that R. Hillel, who was among those who sanctified by sighting according to the true conjunction—",
"and since we hear from Maimonides in the Laws of Sanctification of the Month, beginning of ch. 6 and 15, that knowledge of the true [conjunction] begins from the mean one in the mean motion, it is confirmed that he also knew the mean conjunctions in his time—",
"reckoned all the mean conjunctions that had occurred from his days backward to the end of the count to creation that he gathered from the years counted in the Torah, in the Prophets, and in the words of our rabbis,",
"all of them as he found them current in the world, for there is indeed no way to resolve their doubts, as we mentioned in our previous words;",
"and at the end of this count of his, agreed upon as stated, the sign BHRD resulted for him on the basis of 1 day, 12 hours, 793 parts, which is a uniform measure for all mean conjunctions backward and forward, and he transmitted it to us as a root.",
"And exactly the same holds had he then agreed to count the years to creation fewer or more:",
"so without doubt would his calculation have been completed and his sign given as befitted that calculation,",
